---
title: Transfer Model Attributes to True-Shape Links
subtitle: Pass-through chain dissolution → direct coordinate-join match → nearest-constituent attribute resolution
description: Model links are dissolved across pass-through (unsnapped) node chains, then each physical link piece from 02_create_link.qmd is matched to its dissolved chain via a direct, direction-sensitive (A,B) coordinate join — no graph traversal or synthetic geometry involved. Every piece's real geometry is retained regardless of match outcome; attributes are resolved via nearest-constituent-to-centroid distance and left blank when unmatched.

## Load Data

### Model Links

Filtered the same way `01_node_classification.qmd` filters when it computes
`NeighborCount`/`is_topo_passthrough`: `(LN_2027 > 0 OR FT_2027 IN (70, 80))
AND FT_2027 NOT IN (1, 37, 38, 39)`. Centroid connectors (FT=1) and
non-physical HOV/Managed-Access links (FT=37,38,39) are excluded outright;
everything else must additionally have at least one lane by 2027 to count
as part of today's (or 2027's) connectivity graph — a link coded zero-lane
in 2027 doesn't yet exist as a driveable connection, even if a physical
centerline sits near its geometry. Fixed transit (FT 70/80) is the one
exception to the lane-count rule: rail links carry `LN_2027==0` by
definition (no vehicle lanes), so requiring `LN_2027>0` would silently drop
every rail model link before Part A ever sees it. This match matters beyond
just filtering consistently: if this notebook's dissolve graph could see an
edge that `01` didn't count (or vice versa), a node `01` classified
pass-through (`NeighborCount==2`) could turn out to have a 3rd neighbor
here — and `dissolve_pseudonodes`'s walk, trusting the `NeighborCount==2`
guarantee, would silently take the wrong edge through it. `LN_2027`/`FT_2027`
themselves are reported unchanged on matched output — this only affects
whether a chain counts as connected, not what gets displayed.

```{python}
gdf_links = gpd.read_file(
    PATHS["in_network_links"],
    where="(LN_2027 > 0 OR FT_2027 IN (70, 80)) AND FT_2027 NOT IN (1, 37, 38, 39)",
).to_crs(CRS_UTM)

for col in ("DIRECTION",):
    if col in gdf_links.columns:
        gdf_links[col] = gdf_links[col].str.strip()

print(f"Model links (filtered): {len(gdf_links):,} | CRS: {gdf_links.crs}")
print(f"FT_2027 distribution:\n{gdf_links['FT_2027'].value_counts().sort_index().to_string()}")
```

### Snapped Nodes

Stage 2 guarantees every `link_pieces.gpkg` boundary is already a snap point,
so Stage 3 needs *which* nodes are snapped (split points) versus not. For the
"not" side, `is_topo_passthrough` from `nodes_classified.gpkg`
(`NeighborCount==2`, regardless of FT, lane count, or link-class/designation
uniformity) is safe to silently walk through and absorb into a multi-hop
chain in Part A — a node with exactly two distinct neighbors has exactly one
way to continue through it, full stop, no matter what changes there on the
model side. An unsnapped node that fails even that (3+ neighbors — a real
junction) is *not* pass-through: `dissolve_pseudonodes`'s single-preferred-edge
walk has no reliable way to know which of several real branches continues the
correct chain, so treating every unsnapped node as pass-through (as an
earlier version of this notebook did) silently produced wrong-branch chains
at those nodes. Only 2-neighbor nodes are dissolved through; any 3+-neighbor
unsnapped node is left as a hard chain boundary, and pieces touching it
honestly fail to match rather than getting attributed from a guessed
direction.

This is deliberately broader than `is_pseudo` (which additionally requires
uniform FT and uniform lane count, because it also gates Stage 1 snapping
eligibility — a snap *target* needs that stricter guarantee). Stage 3 only
needs the topological guarantee: real FT-transition, lane-transition, and
link-class-transition nodes have no physical vertex of their own in the
UGRC/UDOT centerlines (arcpy only cuts at genuine junctions), so treating
them as hard chain boundaries here — while `is_pseudo` correctly still sends
them to snapping in `01_node_classification.qmd` — was silently splitting one
physical piece across a model chain boundary the physical network was never
actually cut at. See `_plan/freeway-endpoint-pool-diagnosis.md` and the
node-30208 (Antelope Island Causeway) example that first surfaced this.

`FixedTransit_Rail`-snapped nodes are **included** in `snapped_node_ids` —
since `02_create_link.qmd` Part F now splits the dissolved GTFS rail shapes
at exactly these station coordinates, they are legitimate physical split
points for rail pieces, and must be in the `(A,B)` coordinate-join lookup
below for a rail model-link chain to ever match a rail piece. Nothing about
the match logic itself is rail-aware — it's the same generic coordinate
join used for road pieces.

```{python}
gdf_nodes_snapped = gpd.read_file(PATHS["in_node_snapped"], layer="nodes_snapped").to_crs(CRS_UTM)

snapped_mask = gdf_nodes_snapped["snapped"].fillna(False).astype(bool)
snapped_node_ids = set(gdf_nodes_snapped.loc[snapped_mask, "N"].astype(int))
n_snapped = len(snapped_node_ids)
print(f"Nodes: {len(gdf_nodes_snapped):,} total | {n_snapped:,} snapped (road + rail) ({n_snapped/len(gdf_nodes_snapped):.1%})")

# Snap coordinate lookup: N → (x_round, y_round)
node_coord_lookup: dict[int, tuple[float, float]] = {
    int(row["N"]): (float(row["snapped_x_round"]), float(row["snapped_y_round"]))
    for _, row in gdf_nodes_snapped[snapped_mask].iterrows()
}

# Reverse lookup: (x_round, y_round) → N — used to identify each piece's endpoints.
coord_to_node: dict[tuple[float, float], int] = {v: k for k, v in node_coord_lookup.items()}

print(f"Snap coord lookup: {len(node_coord_lookup):,} entries")
print(f"Reverse coord→node lookup: {len(coord_to_node):,} entries")
```

CC attachment nodes and external station nodes add their own coordinates
here too, restricted to `use_as_split` (computed in
`01_node_classification.qmd`: resolved within 100 m, and not already snapped
by the main pipeline above). `02_create_link.qmd` Part C splits
`link_pieces.gpkg` at exactly this same set, using the same `x_snap`/`y_snap`
values rounded the same way — so a piece boundary exists for every one of
these coordinates to match against. Nodes that don't resolve, or that
coincide with a node already snapped by the main pipeline, are left out
entirely (no coordinate, no split, same as any other unsnapped node).

CC/external connectors that land inline on a single rail mode (no real
junction — `LinkFTCount == 1 & LinkLNCount == 1` restricted to
`FixedTransit` nodes, computed and patched to `is_topo_passthrough = True`
in `01_node_classification.qmd`) must not be re-added to `snapped_node_ids`
here either. That set is unioned into `snapped_node_ids` unconditionally
below; without this exclusion, a rail-inline CC/ext node would be forced
back into `snapped_node_ids` regardless of the `01_node_classification.qmd`
patch, re-imposing exactly the hard chain boundary that patch was meant to
remove — undoing the fix that lets Stage 3's dissolve span the same
station-to-station range the physical rail piece (`02_create_link.qmd`
Part F) already spans. The same uniformity check (not just its
degree-2-restricted `is_pseudo` subset) also covers genuine 3+-neighbor
rail junctions (wyes/crossovers) that `01_node_classification.qmd` force-set
to `is_topo_passthrough = True` — those were never in `cc_ext_split_ids` to
begin with, so this intersection is a no-op for them; they rely entirely on
`pseudo_ids` (below) picking up `is_topo_passthrough` from
`nodes_classified.gpkg` directly.

```{python}
gdf_nodes_classified = gpd.read_file(PATHS["in_node_classified"]).to_crs(CRS_UTM)

gdf_cc_snapped  = gpd.read_file(PATHS["in_node_snapped"], layer="cc_nodes_snapped").to_crs(CRS_UTM)
gdf_ext_snapped = gpd.read_file(PATHS["in_node_snapped"], layer="ext_nodes_snapped").to_crs(CRS_UTM)

cc_ext_split_ids = (
    set(gdf_cc_snapped.loc[gdf_cc_snapped["use_as_split"], "N"].astype(int))
    | set(gdf_ext_snapped.loc[gdf_ext_snapped["use_as_split"], "N"].astype(int))
)
rail_inline_cc_ext_ids = set(
    gdf_nodes_classified.loc[
        gdf_nodes_classified["N"].isin(cc_ext_split_ids)
        & (gdf_nodes_classified["LinkFTCount"] == 1)
        & (gdf_nodes_classified["LinkLNCount"] == 1)
        & gdf_nodes_classified["FixedTransit"],
        "N",
    ].astype(int)
)

attach_coord_lookup: dict[int, tuple[float, float]] = {
    int(row["N"]): (round(float(row["x_snap"]), 2), round(float(row["y_snap"]), 2))
    for _, row in pd.concat([
        gdf_cc_snapped[gdf_cc_snapped["use_as_split"]],
        gdf_ext_snapped[gdf_ext_snapped["use_as_split"]],
    ]).iterrows()
    if int(row["N"]) not in rail_inline_cc_ext_ids
}

node_coord_lookup.update(attach_coord_lookup)
coord_to_node.update({v: k for k, v in attach_coord_lookup.items()})
snapped_node_ids |= set(attach_coord_lookup)

print(f"CC attachment + external station split points added: {len(attach_coord_lookup):,}")
print(f"  ({len(rail_inline_cc_ext_ids):,} rail-inline CC/external node(s) excluded — left as ordinary pass-through)")
print(f"Snap coord lookup now: {len(node_coord_lookup):,} entries")
```

```{python}
pseudo_ids = set(gdf_nodes_classified.loc[gdf_nodes_classified["is_topo_passthrough"], "N"].astype(int))

n_pseudo_snapped = len(pseudo_ids & snapped_node_ids)
print(f"Topological pass-through nodes (NeighborCount==2, any FT/LN/class): {len(pseudo_ids):,}")
print(f"  of which already snapped (expect only pre-existing ~0 cases; CC/external mid-link nodes were already patched to False in 01_node_classification.qmd): {n_pseudo_snapped:,}")
```

```{python}
# Spot-check: round-trip a handful of known snapped nodes through both lookups.
import random
sample_ns = random.sample(sorted(snapped_node_ids), 3)
for n in sample_ns:
    coord = node_coord_lookup[n]
    back = coord_to_node.get(coord)
    print(f"N={n} -> {coord} -> N={back}  {'OK' if back == n else 'MISMATCH'}")
```

```{python}
gdf_pieces = gpd.read_file(PATHS["in_link_pieces"]).to_crs(CRS_UTM)
print(f"Link pieces: {len(gdf_pieces):,} | CRS: {gdf_pieces.crs}")
```

---

## Part A — Pass-Through Chain Dissolve

Collapse chains of model links connected through **pass-through nodes** —
the topological pass-through set (`pass_through_ids = pseudo_ids -
snapped_node_ids`; the subtraction is defensive, these nodes are never
snapped by design — see `01_node_classification.qmd`'s `is_topo_passthrough`).
A node only qualifies if it has exactly two distinct neighbors
(`NeighborCount==2`) — that alone is the guarantee the walk needs to be safe:
at a 2-neighbor node there is exactly one way to continue the chain, so
`dissolve_pseudonodes`'s preferred-else-first-found edge choice can't pick
wrong, regardless of whether FT, lane count, or link class (freeway/ramp/
surface designation) changes there. Only a real 3+-way junction — where
topology alone can't say which branch continues the same physical road — is
**not** pass-through here: it's a hard chain boundary, same as a snapped
node. Pieces whose real physical boundary sits at such a junction will fail
to match (`endpoints_only`/`a_only`/`b_only`) rather than silently being
attributed via a guessed branch.

Each dissolved chain spans from one snapped node (or real junction) to
another; pass-through nodes along the way are absorbed regardless of any
attribute change there. Every model link attribute column (besides `A`, `B`,
geometry) rides along onto the dissolved output, taken from each chain's
first constituent link — this default is only provisional here; Part C
replaces it with a nearest-centroid resolution for multi-constituent chains.

Unlike the old strict-pseudonode set, `FT_2027`/`LN_2027` uniformity across a
chain's constituents is **no longer** guaranteed by construction — a chain
can now legitimately walk through a real FT- or lane-transition node.
`invariant_cols=()` reflects that: both columns go through the same
disagreement check as everything else, and a disagreement is expected and
informational (Part C's nearest-centroid resolution is what actually decides
which constituent's attributes a given physical piece gets), not a bug.

```{python}
pass_through_ids = pseudo_ids - snapped_node_ids
print(f"Pass-through ids (is_topo_passthrough): {len(pseudo_ids):,}")
print(f"Pass-through (unsnapped) ids: {len(pass_through_ids):,}")
```

```{python}
print("Dissolving pass-through chains …")
gdf_dissolved = dissolve_pseudonodes(gdf_links, pass_through_ids, invariant_cols=())

print(f"Original links:   {len(gdf_links):,}")
print(f"Dissolved links:  {len(gdf_dissolved):,}  ({len(gdf_links)-len(gdf_dissolved):,} fewer)")
print()
print("Constituent count distribution:")
print(gdf_dissolved["n_constituents"].value_counts().sort_index().head(10).to_string())
print()
multi = (gdf_dissolved["n_constituents"] > 1).sum()
print(f"Multi-constituent chains: {multi:,} ({multi/len(gdf_dissolved):.1%})")
```

```{python}
disagreement_counts = gdf_dissolved.attrs.get("disagreement_counts", {})
if disagreement_counts:
    print(f"Columns with constituent disagreement in multi-constituent chains ({len(disagreement_counts)}):")
    for col, cnt in sorted(disagreement_counts.items(), key=lambda kv: -kv[1]):
        print(f"  {col:15s}: {cnt:,} chain(s)")
else:
    print("No constituent disagreements found in any multi-constituent chain.")
```

---

## Part B — Piece-to-Chain Match

Stage 2 guarantees every `link_pieces.gpkg` boundary is already a snap point,
so matching a piece to the dissolved chain it belongs to no longer needs any
graph search — it's a direct coordinate lookup followed by a vectorized
`(A,B)` join:

1. Look up each piece's `A_piece`/`B_piece` node id from its rounded start/end
   coordinate via `coord_to_node` (built in Part A's node-loading section).
   A piece with an unsnapped endpoint (e.g. a network-boundary edge) simply
   gets a null on that side — that's expected, not an error.
2. `merge1` matches pieces drawn in the *same* direction as a dissolved chain
   (`A_piece,B_piece == A,B` — "forward"). `merge2` matches pieces drawn in
   the *opposite* direction (`B_piece,A_piece == A,B` — "reverse"). Both can
   legitimately match the same physical piece: a typical two-way street is
   coded as two separate model-link rows (one per direction), each dissolving
   to its own `A,B` chain, so one physical piece produces **two** output rows
   — one per direction. A one-way road (e.g. a freeway, already digitized as
   a separate line per direction) matches only one side, producing one row.

```{python}
gdf_pieces["A_piece"] = pd.Series(
    list(zip(gdf_pieces["x_start"], gdf_pieces["y_start"])), index=gdf_pieces.index
).map(coord_to_node).astype("Int64")
gdf_pieces["B_piece"] = pd.Series(
    list(zip(gdf_pieces["x_end"], gdf_pieces["y_end"])), index=gdf_pieces.index
).map(coord_to_node).astype("Int64")

n_a = gdf_pieces["A_piece"].notna().sum()
n_b = gdf_pieces["B_piece"].notna().sum()
n_both = (gdf_pieces["A_piece"].notna() & gdf_pieces["B_piece"].notna()).sum()
print(f"Pieces with snapped A endpoint:     {n_a:,} / {len(gdf_pieces):,}")
print(f"Pieces with snapped B endpoint:     {n_b:,} / {len(gdf_pieces):,}")
print(f"Pieces with both endpoints snapped: {n_both:,} / {len(gdf_pieces):,}")

# Endpoint-status QA column — carried through to the final export regardless
# of match outcome, so an unattributed piece's geometry is still explainable.
gdf_pieces["endpoint_status"] = np.select(
    [
        gdf_pieces["A_piece"].notna() & gdf_pieces["B_piece"].notna(),
        gdf_pieces["A_piece"].notna() & gdf_pieces["B_piece"].isna(),
        gdf_pieces["A_piece"].isna() & gdf_pieces["B_piece"].notna(),
    ],
    ["both_snapped", "a_only", "b_only"],
    default="neither",
)
print(gdf_pieces["endpoint_status"].value_counts().to_string())
```

```{python}
# Only both-snapped pieces can possibly match an (A,B) chain — gdf_dissolved's
# A/B are never null. Filtering first (rather than merging on a nullable Int64
# key directly) sidesteps a pandas merge/factorize incompatibility with pd.NA.
both_snapped = gdf_pieces[gdf_pieces["A_piece"].notna() & gdf_pieces["B_piece"].notna()].copy()
both_snapped["A_piece"] = both_snapped["A_piece"].astype("int64")
both_snapped["B_piece"] = both_snapped["B_piece"].astype("int64")

merge1 = both_snapped.merge(
    gdf_dissolved,
    left_on=["A_piece", "B_piece"], right_on=["A", "B"],
    how="inner", suffixes=("_piece", "_link"),
)
merge1["piece_direction"] = "forward"

merge2 = both_snapped.merge(
    gdf_dissolved,
    left_on=["B_piece", "A_piece"], right_on=["A", "B"],
    how="inner", suffixes=("_piece", "_link"),
)
merge2["piece_direction"] = "reverse"

matched = pd.concat([merge1, merge2], ignore_index=True)
n_matched_pieces = matched["piece_id"].nunique()
n_dual = matched["piece_id"].value_counts().eq(2).sum()
print(f"Matched rows: {len(matched):,}  (forward {len(merge1):,} + reverse {len(merge2):,})")
print(f"Distinct pieces matched: {n_matched_pieces:,} / {len(gdf_pieces):,}")
print(f"Pieces matched in both directions (two-way streets): {n_dual:,}")
```

```{python}
# Spot-check: a piece matched in both directions should show opposite A/B per row.
if n_dual > 0:
    dual_piece_id = matched["piece_id"].value_counts().eq(2).idxmax()
    print(matched.loc[matched["piece_id"] == dual_piece_id, ["piece_id", "A_piece", "B_piece", "A", "B", "piece_direction"]].to_string(index=False))
```

---

## Part C — Nearest-Constituent Attribute Resolution

`matched` can legitimately contain more than one candidate chain for the same
`(piece_id, piece_direction)` — not only because a chain's own
`constituent_ab_pairs` may span multiple original hops, but because
`gdf_dissolved` itself can contain multiple distinct chains sharing the same
`(A,B)`: self-loop branches (different loop roads that both start and end at
the same real node) and genuine parallel paths (a direct link and a separate
multi-hop alternate between the same two snapped nodes) both produce this.
Node ids alone can't disambiguate either case — only geometry can. A single
rule handles both: explode every candidate chain's constituent hops, join
each hop to `gdf_links` for its attributes and geometry, measure distance
from the piece's centroid to each hop, and keep the global nearest hop per
`(piece_id, piece_direction)` group. This simultaneously selects the correct
candidate chain *and* the correct constituent's attributes within it — a
single-constituent, single-candidate group has exactly one hop and trivially
"wins" regardless of distance.

```{python}
matched = matched.reset_index(drop=True)
matched["match_id"] = matched.index
matched["_pairs"] = matched["constituent_ab_pairs"].apply(json.loads)
matched["_piece_centroid"] = matched.geometry.centroid

exploded = matched[["match_id", "piece_id", "piece_direction", "_pairs"]].explode(
    "_pairs", ignore_index=True
)
exploded["hop_A"] = exploded["_pairs"].str[0].astype("int64")
exploded["hop_B"] = exploded["_pairs"].str[1].astype("int64")
exploded = exploded.drop(columns="_pairs")

# Safe as an exact-key join: gdf_links has zero duplicate directed (A,B) pairs.
gdf_links_idx = gdf_links.set_index(["A", "B"])
exploded = exploded.join(gdf_links_idx, on=["hop_A", "hop_B"])

centroid_lookup = matched.set_index("match_id")["_piece_centroid"]
exploded["piece_centroid"] = exploded["match_id"].map(centroid_lookup)

exploded["dist_to_centroid"] = shapely.distance(
    exploded["geometry"].to_numpy(), exploded["piece_centroid"].to_numpy()
)

print(
    f"Exploded constituent-hop candidates: {len(exploded):,} "
    f"(from {matched['match_id'].nunique():,} matched chain rows, "
    f"{matched[['piece_id','piece_direction']].drop_duplicates().shape[0]:,} distinct piece/direction groups)"
)
```

```{python}
group_sizes = exploded.groupby(["piece_id", "piece_direction"]).size()
n_ambiguous = (group_sizes > 1).sum()
print(f"(piece_id, piece_direction) groups with >1 candidate hop/chain: {n_ambiguous:,} / {len(group_sizes):,}")

best_idx = exploded.groupby(["piece_id", "piece_direction"])["dist_to_centroid"].idxmin()
resolved_attrs = exploded.loc[best_idx].copy()
print(f"Resolved rows: {len(resolved_attrs):,} (one per piece/direction group, as expected)")
assert len(resolved_attrs) == len(group_sizes)
```

```{python}
# Solo-candidate groups (no ambiguity) must always keep their only hop.
solo_groups = group_sizes[group_sizes == 1].index
solo_mask = exploded.set_index(["piece_id", "piece_direction"]).index.isin(solo_groups)
solo_rows = exploded[solo_mask]
print(f"Solo-candidate groups: {len(solo_rows):,}")
print(f"  all present unchanged in resolved_attrs: {solo_rows.index.isin(best_idx).all()}")
```

```{python}
# Spot-check the 4 pieces identified during T7 verification as having >2 raw
# matches (self-loop / parallel-path duplicates) — each should now resolve to
# exactly one row per direction.
for pid in [1443, 336, 11353, 1264]:
    sub = resolved_attrs[resolved_attrs["piece_id"] == pid]
    raw_n = (matched["piece_id"] == pid).sum()
    hops = ", ".join(f"{d}:({a},{b})" for d, a, b in zip(sub["piece_direction"], sub["hop_A"], sub["hop_B"]))
    print(f"piece_id={pid}: {raw_n} raw candidate rows -> {len(sub)} resolved row(s) [{hops}]")
```

```{python}
# Attach piece geometry/lineage + chain-level bookkeeping back onto the
# resolved attribute rows. The piece's own geometry (not the hop geometry,
# already spent computing dist_to_centroid) and UGRC-sourced attributes win
# any name collision with the TDM model attributes carried from gdf_links
# (e.g. both have a differently-sourced ONEWAY column) via explicit suffixes.
piece_base = gdf_pieces.set_index("piece_id")

chain_meta = matched.set_index("match_id")[["A", "B", "n_constituents", "constituent_ab_pairs"]]

gdf_matched_resolved = (
    resolved_attrs.drop(columns="geometry")
    .set_index(["piece_id", "piece_direction"])
    .join(piece_base, on="piece_id", lsuffix="_tdm", rsuffix="_ugrc")
    .join(chain_meta, on="match_id")
    .reset_index()
)
gdf_matched_resolved["trueshape_method"] = "matched"
gdf_matched_resolved = gpd.GeoDataFrame(gdf_matched_resolved, geometry="geometry", crs=CRS_UTM)

print(f"gdf_matched_resolved: {len(gdf_matched_resolved):,} rows | null geometries: {gdf_matched_resolved.geometry.isna().sum()}")
```

---

## Part D — Assemble Final Output and Export

Every piece's geometry is retained regardless of match outcome — pieces with
no matching chain (unsnapped endpoint, or a snapped endpoint pair with no
corresponding model-link chain) keep exactly one row with blank attribute
columns and `trueshape_method="unattributed"`. **No synthetic/straight-line
geometry is ever generated** — this was the old BFS mechanism's failure mode
and the entire reason for this rewrite.

```{python}
# Drop T8's internal computation-only columns before export.
gdf_matched_final = gdf_matched_resolved.drop(
    columns=["match_id", "hop_A", "hop_B", "piece_centroid", "dist_to_centroid"]
)

matched_piece_ids = set(gdf_matched_resolved["piece_id"])
gdf_unmatched = gdf_pieces[~gdf_pieces["piece_id"].isin(matched_piece_ids)].copy()
gdf_unmatched = gdf_unmatched.rename(columns={"ONEWAY": "ONEWAY_ugrc"})
gdf_unmatched["piece_direction"] = pd.NA
gdf_unmatched["A"] = pd.NA
gdf_unmatched["B"] = pd.NA
gdf_unmatched["n_constituents"] = pd.NA
gdf_unmatched["constituent_ab_pairs"] = pd.NA
gdf_unmatched["trueshape_method"] = "unattributed"

# Blank TDM attribute columns (ONEWAY_tdm, FT_2027, etc.) — present in the
# matched table, absent here since no chain claimed these pieces.
tdm_only_cols = [c for c in gdf_matched_final.columns if c not in gdf_unmatched.columns]
for col in tdm_only_cols:
    gdf_unmatched[col] = pd.NA
gdf_unmatched = gdf_unmatched[gdf_matched_final.columns]

print(f"Matched pieces:   {len(matched_piece_ids):,} / {len(gdf_pieces):,}")
print(f"Unmatched pieces: {len(gdf_unmatched):,} / {len(gdf_pieces):,}")
```

Centroid connector links (`02_create_link.qmd` Part E) are not physical-link
pieces at all — no dissolve, no chain match, no `endpoint_status` applies to
them; they arrive already fully attributed from their source model link.
They're aligned to the same output schema and folded in here, exactly like
`gdf_unmatched` above skips Part C's resolution: `ONEWAY` is renamed to
`ONEWAY_tdm` (this is the model's own attribute, the TDM side of the
existing `ONEWAY_tdm`/`ONEWAY_ugrc` split — there is no UGRC centerline
under a centroid connector, so `ONEWAY_ugrc` and every other lineage column
stay blank). `n_constituents`/`constituent_ab_pairs` are filled with their
actual (trivially known, not guessed) values rather than left blank.

```{python}
gdf_centroid_connectors = gpd.read_file(PATHS["in_centroid_connectors"]).to_crs(CRS_UTM)
gdf_centroid_connectors = gdf_centroid_connectors.rename(columns={"ONEWAY": "ONEWAY_tdm"})
gdf_centroid_connectors["length_m"] = gdf_centroid_connectors.geometry.length
gdf_centroid_connectors["piece_direction"] = "forward"
gdf_centroid_connectors["n_constituents"] = 1
gdf_centroid_connectors["constituent_ab_pairs"] = [
    json.dumps([[int(a), int(b)]])
    for a, b in zip(gdf_centroid_connectors["A"], gdf_centroid_connectors["B"])
]

print(f"Centroid connector links: {len(gdf_centroid_connectors):,}")
```

```{python}
gdf_trueshape = pd.concat(
    [gdf_matched_final, gdf_unmatched, gdf_centroid_connectors], ignore_index=True
)
gdf_trueshape = gpd.GeoDataFrame(gdf_trueshape, geometry="geometry", crs=CRS_UTM)
for col in ("A", "B", "n_constituents"):
    gdf_trueshape[col] = gdf_trueshape[col].astype("Int64")

print(f"gdf_trueshape: {len(gdf_trueshape):,} rows")
print(
    f"  = {len(gdf_matched_final):,} matched + {len(gdf_unmatched):,} unmatched "
    f"+ {len(gdf_centroid_connectors):,} centroid connectors"
)
print(f"  vs. {len(gdf_pieces):,} pieces + {len(gdf_matched_final) - len(matched_piece_ids):,} dual-direction extras")
print(f"Null geometries: {gdf_trueshape.geometry.isna().sum()}")
assert len(gdf_trueshape) == (
    len(gdf_pieces)
    + (len(gdf_matched_final) - len(matched_piece_ids))
    + len(gdf_centroid_connectors)
)
assert gdf_trueshape.geometry.isna().sum() == 0
```

Combine `trueshape_method` and `endpoint_status` into a single QA field for
map symbology. `trueshape_method == "matched"` is always a strict subset of
`endpoint_status == "both_snapped"` (Part B's merge only ever runs against
the both-snapped subset of pieces), and `trueshape_method ==
"centroid_connector"` rows have no `endpoint_status` at all (that column
only describes physical-piece endpoint matching), so checking
`trueshape_method` first keeps all six resulting categories non-overlapping:

```{python}
gdf_trueshape["qa_status"] = np.select(
    [
        gdf_trueshape["trueshape_method"] == "centroid_connector",
        gdf_trueshape["trueshape_method"] == "matched",
        gdf_trueshape["endpoint_status"] == "both_snapped",
        gdf_trueshape["endpoint_status"] == "a_only",
        gdf_trueshape["endpoint_status"] == "b_only",
    ],
    ["centroid_connector", "matched", "endpoints_only", "a_only", "b_only"],
    default="neither",
)
print(gdf_trueshape["qa_status"].value_counts().to_string())
```

```{python}
out_path = PATHS["out_links_trueshape"]
out_path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
gdf_trueshape.to_file(out_path, driver="GPKG")
print(f"Saved to: {out_path}")
```
